chunks: 112 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ja'far ibn Isa said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding the dirhams which I know are not valid among Muslims except with a deficiency (wadī'ah), which come to me from some of them without deficiency due to my ignorance of it, and I only took them considering them good? Is it permissible for me to take them and remove them from my hand to him to the extent of what came to me from them?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is not permissible.'

And I wrote to him: 'May I be your ransom, is it permissible if it comes to me to return it to its owner without his knowledge of it, or to substitute it for him while he does not know that I am substituting it for him and returning it to him?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is not permissible.' (507)
113 - From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) that I had dirhams owed to me by a man, and the Sultan annulled those dirhams and brought dirhams higher in value than those first dirhams, and they have a deficiency today. So which is due to me: the first ones that the Sultan annulled, or the dirhams that the Sultan validated? So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The first dirhams.'

key_terms.وَضِيعَةٌ: Deficiency or debasement in the intrinsic value of the coin

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using debased currency (dirhams with wadī'ah) in transactions according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *wadī'ah* (debased currency) by distinguishing between intrinsic deficiency and official recognition. Imam al-Rida (AS) rules that if a debtor owes a specific amount in debased coins and the state validates a newer, higher-denomination coin, the debt remains tied to the original debased currency, preventing the debtor from substituting the new coins to the creditor's detriment. This highlights the Shia principle of preserving the specific value agreed upon in contracts despite fluctuating monetary standards.
